title: Realization and uniqueness for a strict birational group law
statement: Let $B$ be a field or a discrete valuation ring [def-weil-field, def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], and put $S=\operatorname{Spec}B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Products and fibres are scheme-theoretic base changes [def-pc-base-change]. Let $X$ be a smooth separated finite-type $S$-scheme with nonempty fibres [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. An open in an $S$-scheme is $S$-dense if its intersection with each fibre is dense. An $S$-rational map is a morphism on an $S$-dense open, up to equality on an $S$-dense common open; an $S$-birational map is represented by an isomorphism between $S$-dense opens. Let $m:X\times_SX\dashrightarrow X$ be $S$-rational, associative wherever both composites are defined, such that $\Phi(x,y)=(x,m(x,y))$ and $\Psi(x,y)=(m(x,y),y)$ are $S$-birational. The law is called strict if there is an open $D\subseteq X\times_SX$ on which $m$ is defined and $\Phi,\Psi$ induce isomorphisms $D\simeq V$, $D\simeq W$ onto open subschemes, with $D,V,W$ dense in every fibre of each projection $X\times_SX\to X$. Assume the law is strict. There are a smooth separated finite-type $S$-group scheme $H$ and an open immersion $i:X\hookrightarrow H$ with $S$-dense image such that multiplication on $H$ restricts to $m$. Here an $S$-group scheme means a scheme over $S$ with multiplication $H\times_SH\to H$, inverse $H\to H$, and identity $S\to H$ satisfying the associativity, unit, and inverse diagrams. If $(H_1,i_1)$ and $(H_2,i_2)$ are two such pairs, there is a unique $S$-group isomorphism $a:H_1\simeq H_2$ with $a\circ i_1=i_2$.

source.place: BLR 5.2 Theorem 3 and the explicit translate construction of 5.3, printed pp.117-128 (PDF pp.123-134); descent to an arbitrary field or DVR in 6.5 Corollary 2, printed pp.157-158 (PDF pp.163-164); uniqueness in 5.1 Proposition 3; primary scan https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf; local literature copy WANTED.

proof.text: Choose a strict henselization $B'$ of $B$ at its closed point and put $S'=\operatorname{Spec}B'$. The strict-henselization triples give a strictly henselian local ring, and faithful flatness makes $S'\to S$ an fpqc cover (it is affine). If $B$ is a DVR, the triples/colimit comparison identifies $B'$ with the geometric-point strict henselization, so $B'$ is a DVR by the strict-henselization DVR lemma. If $B$ is a field, the triples' maximal-ideal and residue assertions make $B'$ its separable closure. Thus $B'$ is Noetherian and normal; for a DVR, a fraction of negative valuation satisfies no monic equation. Base change of strict laws gives the same hypotheses for $X'=X\times_SS'$ and $m'$.

source.place: 6.5 Corollary 2, first paragraph; Stacks 04GP, 07QM (lemma-dumb-properties-henselization), 0AP3 (lemma-henselization-dvr); Stacks 04GP/04GR comparison of the two constructions

proof.text: Apply the finite translate enlargement to $(X',m')$ over the Noetherian normal strictly henselian ring $B'$. Obtain $j':X'\hookrightarrow Z'$ with $S'$-dense image, a strict law $n'$ on $Z'$ and a representative defined on all of $j'(X')\times_{S'}j'(X')$. The same lemma gives an $S'$-section of $X'$, hence of $Z'$. Apply completion of the dense open square, with $U=j'(X')$, to give $Z'$ its group structure; write $H'=Z'$. It is smooth, separated and finite type, and its multiplication restricts to $m'$.

source.place: 5.3 Lemmas 5-8, especially the paragraph preceding Lemma 8

proof.text: On $S''=S'\times_SS'$, the two pullbacks of $H'$ contain the two pullbacks of $X'$ as fibrewise dense opens by base change. The canonical identification of these copies of $X'$ preserves the rational law (both laws come from $m$). It therefore induces a birational map compatible with multiplication. Rational-homomorphism extension gives a unique group isomorphism $\theta:p_1^*H'\simeq p_2^*H'$ extending it. On $S'''=S'\times_SS'\times_SS'$, the maps $\theta_{23}\theta_{12}$ and $\theta_{13}$ restrict to the same canonical identification on $X_{S'''}$; uniqueness in the extension lemma makes them equal. Thus $\theta$ is a descent datum compatible with the group law. The extension lemma allows arbitrary bases, so neither overlap is assumed to be a field, a DVR or strictly henselian.

source.place: 6.5 Corollary 2, overlap and cocycle paragraph; 5.1 Proposition 3 proof

proof.text: Apply effective descent for smooth groups to the faithfully flat extension $B\to B'$ and the datum just constructed. It gives a smooth separated finite-type $S$-group $H$ with $H_{S'}\simeq H'$. The open $j'(X')\subset H'$ is invariant under its datum by construction of $\theta$. Invariant-open image descent applied to $H'\to H$ yields an open $O\subset H$ with $O_{S'}=j'(X')$, carrying exactly its induced datum. The canonical map $X'\simeq O_{S'}$ intertwines the canonical data of $X$ and $O$. Morphism descent applied to it and its inverse gives inverse isomorphisms $X\simeq O$. Their composites descend identity morphisms and hence are identities by uniqueness. Compose with $O\hookrightarrow H$ to obtain $i:X\hookrightarrow H$.

source.place: 6.5 Theorem 1 and Corollary 2; invariant-open descent and morphism descent

proof.text: For each $s\in S$ choose $s'\in S'$ over it. A nonempty open of $H_s$ pulls back to a nonempty open of $H_{s'}$ by surjectivity of field-extension base change, and hence meets $i(X)_{s'}$, which is dense by construction. Thus $i(X)_s$ is dense. On the domain $D$ in the strictness hypothesis, the morphisms $i\circ m$ and $\mu_H\circ(i\times i)$ have equal pullbacks to $S'$ by step 2. Morphism descent is faithful, so they agree on $D$. This identifies the rational laws and proves existence with the stated finite-type and density properties.

source.place: 6.5 Corollary 2, descent of the dense chart and its law

proof.text: For two pairs $(H_1,i_1)$ and $(H_2,i_2)$, the identification $i_2\circ i_1^{-1}:i_1(X)\simeq i_2(X)$ is an $S$-birational map and respects multiplication on the dense domain representing $m$. Rational-homomorphism extension therefore gives a unique group isomorphism $a:H_1\simeq H_2$ extending it. In particular $a\circ i_1=i_2$ on all of $X$, as required.

source.place: 5.1 Proposition 3 and its proof; 6.5 Corollary 2 uniqueness
